ambiguities.description: Doctor-patient relationship constraints: Line 31 states 'every patient has exactly one primary doctor,' and line 7 states 'each appointment is with exactly one doctor.' It is not explicit whether an appointment must be with the patient's primary doctor, or whether a patient can be seen by any doctor. If a patient can see a different doctor, should there be a constraint that 'a patient can have multiple doctors across different appointments'? If the appointment doctor must match the primary doctor, should a subset or equality constraint be expressed?

source_references.excerpt: Each appointment is with exactly one doctor.
Yes, every patient has exactly one primary doctor. That's separate from who they happen to see in a given appointment.

ambiguities.description: Temporal scope of appointment status: The appointment status value constraint lists 'scheduled, checked-in, completed, cancelled.' It is not specified whether a single appointment can have its status change over time (e.g., from scheduled → checked-in → completed), or whether status is static. If status changes are tracked, should the model include a timestamp or history? The current model treats status as a single current value.

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment also has a status. The status is one of: scheduled, checked-in, completed, or cancelled. ... An appointment always has exactly one status from that list.

ambiguities.description: Visit reason optionality: Line 27 states 'An appointment can have a visit reason the patient gives when booking.' The use of 'can have' suggests optionality, meaning an appointment can exist without a visit reason. Is this correct, or is it assumed all appointments have a reason recorded?

source_references.excerpt: An appointment can have a visit reason the patient gives when booking

ambiguities.description: Follow-up note optionality and attribution: Line 27 states 'after the visit the doctor can attach a follow-up note' and 'at most one follow-up note per appointment.' The phrasing suggests a follow-up note is optional and only attached after a visit completes. However, it is unclear whether a follow-up note is mandatory for completed appointments, or entirely optional even for completed appointments.

source_references.excerpt: after the visit the doctor can attach a follow-up note. At most one follow-up note per appointment.

ambiguities.description: Appointment cancellation constraints: The status value includes 'cancelled,' but there is no discussion of what happens to a cancelled appointment or whether cancellation has business impact (e.g., the date/time slot becomes available again, or the doctor is notified). The model does not capture any cancellation-specific semantics.

source_references.excerpt: The status is one of: scheduled, checked-in, completed, or cancelled.

ambiguities.description: Date and TimeSlot representation: Lines 19 specifies that appointments are 'on a date and at a time slot' with examples like '09:00 or 09:30'. It is not clear whether TimeSlot is a simple time value (HH:MM format) or a reference to a predefined set of available clinic time slots. If predefined, should TimeSlot be modeled as a separate entity type? The current model treats it as a value type.

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment is on a date and at a time slot -- we book in fixed slots like 09:00 or 09:30.
